rows.name: LEDA
rows.reason: Current LEDA provides C++ graph structures and source redistribution rights; retain as later evidence because equivalent open licensing at the 2016 cutoff is unverified.

rows.name: SNAP
rows.reason: SNAP documents BSD C++ directed/undirected graph containers, dynamic structure, attributes and large-network scope. Retain; filtered-workload speed, complete move semantics and high-degree behavior still require verification.

rows.name: LLAMA — mutable multiversioned CSR graph storage
rows.reason: LLAMA's C++11 mutable CSR snapshots/properties support update/analysis workloads. Research engine, not drop-in container; streaming integration unfinished and persistent deletion configuration broken. Directed/undirected convenience APIs and arbitrary mutations remain unverified.

rows.name: SNAP — Stanford Network Analysis Platform
rows.reason: Mutable directed/undirected graphs and templated vertex/edge data support sparse analysis. Custom GLib conventions require integration; historical releases contain breaks/deletion fixes. No workload benchmark or full dependency/license audit performed.

rows.name: OGDF — Open Graph Drawing Framework
rows.reason: OGDF offers C++ graphs, associative arrays and algorithms. GPL conflicts with a permissive-license preference; drawing scope may be unnecessary. Allocation behavior and mutation-heavy workload performance remain unestablished.

rows.name: OGDF (Open Graph Drawing Framework)
rows.reason: OGDF offers C++ graph mutation/attributes; 2023.09 API postdates question. Adjacency-list edge lookup depends on degree. Boost closure/performance unverified; GPL v2/v3 exceptions may fit permissive preferences less well.

rows.name: SNAP (Stanford Network Analysis Platform)
rows.reason: SNAP provides self-contained dynamic C++ graphs with node/edge data and large-network design using GLib-style types. C++11 idioms, filtered-query performance, move semantics and skewed-degree behavior remain unestablished; benchmark workload.

rows.name: Snap / snapd
rows.reason: Snap packages Linux applications, and snapd manages those packages; neither supplies C++ graph representation, graph mutation, or graph algorithms.

rows.name: LEDA
rows.reason: Retain LEDA: current Free Version has 2026 redistribution licensing distinct from former agreements. Blanket proprietary exclusion is unjustified; 2016 licensing, Boost dependency, graph/API configuration and performance remain unverified.

rows.name: LEMON — ListDigraph/ListGraph with selectable graph representations
rows.reason: Mutable graphs/data maps offer representation tradeoffs. Smart types lack arbitrary deletion; StaticDigraph immutable. Mutation can invalidate affected iterators; removed IDs reusable. C++11 style, dependency/license audit and exact publication date unverified.

rows.name: LEMON
rows.reason: LEMON offers permissive C++ graphs with indexed mutable APIs, but retrieval failed. Boost-dependency absence, degree behavior, performance and exact semantics remain unverified; Boost Software License does not establish Boost use.

rows.name: SNAP
rows.reason: Its BSD-licensed C++ core supports directed/undirected graphs, mutable nodes and edges, and attached attributes, directly covering the requested graph representation and manipulation.

rows.name: NetworKit C++ core
rows.reason: Native C++ graph analytics; historical directed graphs/edge attributes supported. Historical mutation/deletion costs, payload ergonomics and significant Boost-dependency absence unverified. Current storage/APIs cannot establish 2016 availability.

rows.name: Snap / snapd
rows.reason: The official source defines snaps as application packages and snapd as their management service. That is a decisive mismatch with the requested C++ graph representation/manipulation library, despite the similar name.
